text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm rolling a tiny TF change to switch service annotations + Gateway TLS passthrough fallback for the inference service as a canary. Need a quick review on secret binding, healthcheck wiring, and probe port mapping.

devon: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/inference/infra/-/merge_requests/312 — main intent is to enable NLB passthrough for TLS and add an explicit healthcheck-port so the LB doesn't hit the app TLS.

devon: Key terraform change: add annotation in k8s_service resource, and GatewayAPI TCPRoute to enable passthrough.

jake: Quick flag: if backend-protocol is `tls` + passthrough, ALB/NLB healthchecks can behave weirdly. If the LB expects HTTP but backend speaks TLS, healthchecks will fail. Are we switching healthchecks to TCP?

maria: We plan to set healthcheck port to 8081 (probe) and use TCP for the LB healthcheck. App serves TLS on 8080. Probe stays plaintext on 8081. Is that safe?

devon: Share of YAML for context:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-svc
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: "tls"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-port: "8081"
spec:
  ports:
  - name: tls
    port: 8080
    targetPort: 8080
  - name: probe
    port: 8081
    targetPort: 8081
  type: ClusterIP
```

jake: Two practical checks:
- Ensure LB healthcheck protocol is TCP for port 8081 so it doesn't try to parse TLS.
- Gateway TLS passthrough will forward raw TLS to pods — confirm the pod is presenting the expected cert (SNI sanity). If SNI mismatch, some LBs will serve default cert and trigger fallback.

maria: Secret wiring: pod mounts k8s secret `inference-tls` at /etc/certs and the app loads it. Gateway config references secret `inference-gateway-tls` in the same ns. Will that mismatch cause termination with a default cert?

devon: If Gateway is in passthrough mode it should not terminate, but some Gateway implementations still have a secret for edge termination as a fallback. The pod-level cert must have SANs that match client SNI. If gateway presents a fallback cert before forwarding, clients see that.

maria: Noted. I'll make sure cert SANs include the external hostname and add a short note in rollout doc.

maria: Also adding this probe-related annotation to the TF change: `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-protocol: tcp` — is that ok?

jake: Yeah, tcp is the safe option here. One nit: if we want to preserve client IP for logs, we need `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` on Service and NLB target type `node`. That impacts autoscaling and pod distribution — do we need preserve-client-ip?

maria: We don't strictly need preserve-client-ip for this service. Leave externalTrafficPolicy default (Cluster).

ops-bot: Deploy check: canary target=5% for infra change -> infra oncall notified. No quota or cert expiry blockers. :white_check_mark:

jake: LGTM for the secret wiring + tcp healthcheck. Small suggestion: add `readinessProbe`/`livenessProbe` notes in the rollout doc showing probe endpoints and that they are plaintext.

maria: Done — I pushed the doc update and added PR comment. PR now: https://git.redwood.ai/r/inference/infra/-/merge_requests/312. I'll monitor canary for 10m and check `kubectl get endpoints` + `aws elbv2 describe-target-health`.

devon: I'll keep an eye on the target health and gateway logs. If we see TLS handshake failures, rollback and switch to ALB termination + reissue certs.

maria: Thanks all :pray:
